parameters.text:
=You prepare the variable parts of a first-contact B2B email from {{ $('Read Settings').first().json['Sender Name'] }}, {{ $('Read Settings').first().json['Sender Title'] }} at Texprove, to {{ $json['Contact Name'] || '(no named contact)' }} ({{ $json['Contact Title'] || 'title unknown' }}) at {{ $json.Company }}. Do NOT write a full email. The greeting, the value sentence, the offer of a 30-minute live demo with the calendar link, the sign-off, the signature and the opt-out line are fixed text that code adds around your parts.

Language of everything you write: {{ ['turkey','türkiye','turkiye'].includes(String($json.Country || '').trim().toLowerCase()) ? 'Turkish (natural business Turkish, not a translation)' : 'English' }}.
Audience: {{ /^(marka|brand)$/i.test(String($json.Segment || '').trim()) ? 'a BRAND that is legally accountable for its supplier data' : 'an EXPORTER / MANUFACTURER whose EU customers ask for Digital Product Passport and compliance data' }}.
Recipient's role: {{ $json['Contact Role'] || 'unknown' }}. For a decision maker lean on the business side (answering EU customers once, keeping the customer); for a data owner (sustainability, compliance, quality, certification) lean on the practical side (existing data is imported, Excel or API, no ERP change).
Verified fact about the company: {{ $json['Personalisation Hook'] }}
The fixed sentence that follows your opening is: {{ /^(marka|brand)$/i.test(String($json.Segment || '').trim()) ? ($('Read Settings').first().json['Value Prop Brand EN'] || '') : ($('Read Settings').first().json['Value Prop Exporter EN'] || '') }} Do not repeat it.

Return JSON with these keys:
- person_full_name: the contact's full name with normal capitalisation, ONLY if the Contact Name above is a real person's name. Empty string if it is empty, a job title, a role, a department or a placeholder (for example "General Manager", "Export Contact", "Sales Team", anything containing "/").
- person_first_name: that person's first name, or empty string.
- company_short: the company's everyday name without legal suffixes (drop "San. ve Tic. A.Ş.", "Ltd. Şti.", "Dış Ticaret", text in brackets), for example "Yusteks Tekstil".
- opening: ONE sentence, at most 30 words, personal to this company and based only on the verified fact, showing that we looked at them specifically. No greeting, nothing about Texprove, no question.
- support: {{ /^(marka|brand)$/i.test(String($json.Segment || '').trim()) ? 'empty string (brands get a fixed text)' : 'one or two sentences, at most 45 words in total, built only from the approved messages below, choosing what fits this company and this role' }}.
- subject: {{ /^(marka|brand)$/i.test(String($json.Segment || '').trim()) ? 'empty string (brands get a fixed subject)' : 'at most 7 words, plain, about Digital Product Passport or compliance data for their EU customers; no hype, no question mark' }}.

Approved messages for exporters (use only these, lightly rephrased; add no other claims):
- Today the same certificate, report and audit data is prepared again for every customer; in Texprove it is organised once and reused for every customer.
- You do not start from scratch: you import your existing data and can export it any time; your data stays yours.
- Texprove is a GS1 Türkiye solution partner.
- The EU forced labour ban applies from 14 December 2027. The textile Digital Product Passport rules are expected in 2027 (never give a fixed date). Textile EPR national schemes are due by April 2028; that obligation sits with the brand, so to an exporter say "for your customer, the brand".

Never write: prices or package names, percentages or savings rates, "fewer audits", Tier claims, a catalog or a sample, a video, a call or a meeting, 15 minutes, any link or web address, competitor figures, any date other than the three above. Never mention the company's customers, buyers or the brands or retailers it supplies by name, nor order volumes, quantities, capacities, margins or revenue, even if that is public; if the verified fact contains such details, refer to it in general terms (for example "your exports to European retailers").

parameters.content:
## Compliance gate
Plain JavaScript, no AI. Blocks: empty email, free/personal domain, opted-out, email or domain on the Suppression tab (İYS "ret" opt-outs and manual do-not-contact entries), email domain not matching website, country not in the allowed list (Turkey, Bangladesh, Vietnam, Malaysia, Brazil: the countries the dashboard can pick). İYS itself is not queried: Nil exports İYS opt-outs into the Suppression tab. Add more rules here after Nil confirms KVKK / İYS requirements.

## Settings, Suppression and extra columns
Settings: one row with columns Sender Name, Sender Title, Company Legal Name, Company Address, Opt-out TR, Opt-out EN, Nil Email. Optional: Sheet URL, HubSpot Monthly Limit (default 3000), HubSpot Pause Percent (default 80).
Suppression tab: Email | Domain | Reason | Date (one row per address or domain never to contact).
Leads needs a Draft Body EN column. Log tab: Timestamp | Workflow | Lead ID | Company | Step | Input | Output | Reason.

## Draft check, English copy, log
Plain code, no AI: every draft must contain the sender name, legal name, address, the opt-out sentence in its language, the data-source sentence, no links except the lead's website, no hype words, and nothing commercially sensitive (buyer or brand names, money, quantities, order/price/capacity/margin wording). Failures are saved as Compliance Status = "Needs fix" with reasons, for Nil to correct before approving.
"Translate to English" (Claude Haiku 5.5) then writes a plain English copy of Turkish drafts to the Draft Body EN column so Nil can compare; English drafts leave it empty. The compliance decision and the draft are appended to the Log tab.
